newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Rugby Union and its New Zealand counterpart have been approached by the managing director of London's Wembley Stadium concerning a plan by English promoters to stage a Test match between the Wallabies and the All Blacks in November. It is believed the promoters are prepared to pay millions to seal the deal. Page 20.

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker confirmed yesterday that plans are still alive for a possible Melbourne rugby league team, despite discouraging ticket sales for the State of Origin game to be held at the Melbourne Cricket Ground tonight. Page 20.

Australian cricketer Michael Bevan is under siege as it appears the England team has worked out how to get him out: bounce him with two gullys and a short ball until he is dismissed. While Bevan is a talented player in one-day matches he appears to lack onfidence when batting in Tests. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The two coaches in tonight's State of Origin game - New South Wales' Tom Raudonikis and Queensland's Paul Vautin - have gone head to head after Vautin claimed yesterday the 1997 series may be the last. Raudonikis said the prediction was "absurd". Page 46

Australian Socceroo Graham Arnold has always been a team player, often doing the work of players 10 years younger than himself, but in tonight's World Cup qualifier against the Solomon Islands at Parramatta Stadium he will be playing for himself. Page 46.

Australian world number one golfer Greg Norman announced yesterday he is trading in his private jet for a A$40 million Boeing 737, a commercial aircraft the same as those flown by Qantas and Ansett in Australia. When Norman takes delivery of the aircraft next year it will be equipped with an office, meeting room, private suite and an exercise room. Page 46.
THE AGE

Police have begun an investigation into an incident at a Melbourne nightclub on Sunday involving Collingwood Australian Football League key-position player Aaron James. James will face disciplinary action, and possibly the sack, over the incident. Page B6.

North Melbourne Australian Football League captain Wayne Carey may be back in action against Adelaide at Football Park on Sunday. Roos football manager Geoff Walsh said Carey, who has been out with a shoulder injury, had shown great improvement over the ast three days. Page B16.

Australian tennis player Rachel McQuillan will meet Romania's Irina Spirlea in the second round of the DFS Classic women's grasscourt tournament in Birmingham, England, after defeating Croat Silvia Talaja 6-1, 6-3. Page B14.
THE HERALD SUN

Geelong Australian Football League star Gary Ablett may need to call it a day as he prepares this week to see an orthopaedic surgeon about his troublesome right knee. Ablett has partially torn his anterior cruciate ligament, an injury which may see him ot for the rest of the season. Page 80.

Chris Anstey will come off the bench to start for the Melbourne Magic in tonight's National Basketball League clash against Canberra at Melbourne Park. Veteran player John Dorge is nursing a serious knee injury, and Anstey says he is ready for the responibility of being a starter for the team. Page 71.

Jockey Michael Clark, the winner of 40 Group 1 titles including the Melbourne Cup and the Japan Cup, slipped back into town yesterday to ride for his father at Moe. He will ride at Moonee Valley today on the Robbie Laing-trained Zingaro in the Oceania Hadicap. Page 71.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Manly and North Sydney rugby league teams are apparently close to agreeing on an historic merger, with the full support of the Australian Rugby League. It is expected the merger will take place next year in a likely unified ARL-Super League competition. Page 76.

New South Wales Boxing Association medical officer Dr Lew Lewis, boxer Kostya Tszyu's doctor, said yesterday Tszyu's shock loss of his world boxing title to American Vince Phillips in Atlantic City last week was the result of taking amino acids. Page 74.

Charges of alleged greyhound breeding fraud against Sydney Swans Australian Football League player Tony Lockett may be dropped after Senior Constable Jamie Marra told the Dandenong Magistrates' Court yesterday the prosecution needed more time to examine te evidence provided by Lockett. Page 71.
